messages:
dmitri: noticing a big spike in KV metadata growth right after the midnight batch-config push. pages are filling fast, block_manager is thrashing. anyone oncall?
lydia_sre: oncall here, watching. can you paste the top logs?
dmitri: here's the tail from block_manager:```
[10:02:13Z] block_manager: metadata_entries=3.2M, blocks_open=1248, memory=18.2GB
[10:02:14Z] kv_cache: continuous_batching: inflight_batches=426, avg_tokens=1342
[10:02:14Z] eviction: scanned_blocks=0.2M, evicted=12, failed_evictions=73
[10:02:15Z] block_manager: allocation_error: cannot_allocate_new_block (metadata leak suspected)
```
lydia_sre: that `avg_tokens=1342` looks wrong — our max_batch_tokens was supposed to be 512. who rolled config?
dmitri: @ops-sre pushed a change in autoscale/batching at 09:58 (internal-config). I see: `max_batch_tokens: 4096` accidentally.
ops-sre: yep that was me, trying to reduce small batch overhead. i missed the env flag for paged-kv. rolling back now.
infra-bot: Incident declared: SEV2 - paged-kv metadata growth causing allocation errors (trigger: block_manager allocation_error)
dmitri: customers starting to see higher latencies and a few 5xxs on heavy routing buckets. carol_pm, heads up on impact?
carol_pm: thanks — paging SLO owners. I have a few customers on Dedicated who reported 503s via support. probably related. marking affected customers list now.
ben_oncall: I'm on the night rotation. I'll take lead for mitigation if you want to handoff.
lydia_sre: handoff acknowledged to @ben_oncall. current mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching by reducing max inflight and max_batch_tokens 2) revert the accidental config 3) patch eviction policy to prefer small metadata-only blocks 4) enable temporary aggressive eviction TTL for metadata.
dmitri: immediate command I ran to throttle (rolled back in staging first):```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-config/api/v1/batching -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"max_batch_tokens":512,"max_batch_size":8,"max_inflight_batches":64}'
```
ops-sre: applied rollback to prod at 10:06:02Z. pushing a hotfix to block_manager eviction at 10:08:30Z.
deploy-bot: deploy started: block-manager/eviction-hotfix@v2.3.1 by ops-sre
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: block-manager/eviction-hotfix@v2.3.1 (10:09:12Z)
lydia_sre: post-rollback stats (10:10):```
[10:10:05Z] block_manager: metadata_entries=1.1M, blocks_open=432, memory=8.1GB
[10:10:06Z] kv_cache: inflight_batches=58, avg_tokens=498
[10:10:06Z] eviction: scanned_blocks=12k, evicted=920, failed_evictions=0
```
ben_oncall: seeing latency drop on the affected clusters, 503s reduced to baseline. still monitoring for slow memory leaks.
carol_pm: thanks — i'm updating support threads and notifying customers who reported errors, telling them we rolled back the batch config and deployed an eviction hotfix.
dmitri: we also need a customer-impact assessment doc. quick notes: "~7% of request traffic to heavy-batching endpoints saw 2-4x latency. ~0.8% of requests returned 5xx during the 8-minute window between config push and rollback. Affected: a subset of Dedicated customers and some hosted tenants in us-west-2."
ops-sre: adding quick mitigation followups: 1) add validation guard to config service to cap max_batch_tokens when paged_kv=true 2) enable preflight rollout to 5% for config changes 3) add metric alert for metadata_entries > 2M
lydia_sre: agreed. also add a runbook step: if allocation_error appears, immediately set `max_inflight_batches=32` and `max_batch_tokens=256` until manual assessment.
incident-bot: Handoff note: incident owner changed from dmitri to ben_oncall at 10:12Z.
ben_oncall: taking incident lead. current risk: residual metadata fragments causing slower GC. plan to run a background reclaim job during low traffic window (in 2 hours).
dmitri: can we recreate the leak locally for a test? i have a reproducer that simulates tiny-long sequences and high batch aggregation. posting gist: https://internal-gists/runs/kv-leak-sim
ops-sre: created follow-up ticket INFRA-1729 for config validation + rollout gating. assigned to @ops-sre, priority P1.
carol_pm: I'll coordinate customer comms and postmortem owner. suggest cross-team postmortem with eng-runtime, eng-sre, and product ops.
lydia_sre: quick retrospective notes in thread to capture steps and timeline. we'll expand in the postmortem. good job everyone for fast rollback and targeted eviction patch. :thumbsup:
ben_oncall: leaving a small task list before next handoff: 1) run background reclaim & confirm GC completes 2) verify no further allocation_error logs for 1 hour 3) attach affected tenant IDs to support tickets 4) schedule postmortem.
dmitri: i already started a branch to add config guard and unit tests. will open PR with tests and preflight rollout in 30m.
ops-sre: closing monitoring loop — added alert: `kv.block_manager.metadata_entries > 2_000_000 for 1m` -> pager.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (hotfix/deploy + config rollback) — monitoring for stabilization. incident timeline will be generated from logs.
ben_oncall: handing off monitoring to next oncall at 12:00Z. leave notes in ops runbook. good job everyone.
lydia_sre: acknowledged handoff. I'll watch the reclaim job and escalate if anything regresses.
carol_pm: I'll own the customer postmortem slide and share with legal/support. closing internal incident channel after postmortem is drafted.
ops-sre: moving INFRA-1729 -> in_progress.
ben_oncall: last check at 10:35Z shows metrics stable. closing thread in 1h if no further alerts.
lydia_sre: confirmed no allocation errors since 10:11Z.
incident-bot: Incident closed by ben_oncall at 11:38Z (status: monitoring -> resolved).
ben_oncall: final note: root cause = unvalidated batch config allowing huge batch token caps on paged-kv paths which overwhelmed metadata accounting and prevented timely eviction. fix = config validation + eviction improvements + rollout gating. follow-up owners: ops-sre (config), eng-runtime (eviction), product (customer comms)."
